title: Gold Falls Below $4,100 as Oil Shock Lifts Fed Hike Bets
excerpt: Gold dropped more than 2% to around $4,053, its lowest since August 4, as Brent above $112 kept inflation fears alive ahead of the Fed's October 27-28 meeting.
body:
• Gold fell more than 2% on Thursday to around $4,053 an ounce, its lowest since August 4, after slipping below the $4,100 level that had held in recent sessions.
  • The trigger was oil, not safe-haven demand: attacks on Saudi energy sites and shipping in the Strait of Hormuz pushed Brent above $112 and WTI toward $100, lifting inflation expectations.
  • Traders expect the Federal Reserve to hold at its October 27-28 meeting but price roughly an 86-89% chance of another 25-basis-point hike in December — a mix that raises the cost of holding non-yielding gold.
  • For buyers, the next level to watch is $4,000: a sustained break below $4,063 support opens that mark, while a recovery needs to reclaim about $4,151.

Gold extended losses below $4,100 on Thursday, falling more than 2% to around $4,053 an ounce, its lowest level since August 4, as an energy shock in the Middle East reinforced expectations that U.S. interest rates will stay higher for longer.

The move ran against gold's usual safe-haven pattern. Kitco reported spot gold near $4,086.90 in early U.S. trading, down $53.40 or 1.29%, with spot silver near $55.79, down $2.07 or 3.57%. Prices weakened further as the session progressed, according to FXStreet.

Oil is driving the trade

Fresh attacks linked to the Houthis on Saudi Arabia's Shaybah oil field and King Fahd International Airport, and renewed attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, kept crude elevated. FXStreet put WTI around $98.50, near five-week highs. Kitco put Brent above $112 a barrel, its highest since May, with WTI approaching $100.

Iran claimed seven oil tankers were damaged overnight in the Hormuz waterway, a claim Kitco said had not been independently confirmed in full. The U.S. State Department has ordered non-emergency government employees and family members to leave Saudi Arabia. The New York Times, cited by FXStreet, reported that the United States and Israel have drawn up plans for renewed strikes against Iran after the U.S. midterm elections, potentially targeting energy infrastructure.

Higher crude feeds directly into consumer prices. That makes it harder for the Federal Reserve to bring inflation back toward its 2% target and supports higher bond yields, which increase the opportunity cost of holding gold, an asset that pays no interest.

A hawkish hold, then a December hike bet

Traders look to next week's Fed meeting on October 27-28, where the central bank is widely expected to leave rates unchanged after raising them by 25 basis points in September. The decision itself is not the risk for gold. The guidance is.

FXStreet said the CME FedWatch Tool placed the odds of another hike in December at 89%. Kitco put the likelihood of a 25-basis-point December increase at around 86%, with a high probability of no change in October. U.S. data on Thursday did little to soften that view: weekly initial jobless claims fell by 6,000 to a seasonally adjusted 194,000 in the week ended October 17, below expectations of about 200,000, Kitco reported.

The dollar and yields sent mixed signals. FXStreet put the U.S. Dollar Index around 101.75 after a three-week low of 101.45, and the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield around 5.06%, down more than 1% on the day. Kitco also noted yields falling toward the 5.0% area as technology stocks sold off. Gold fell anyway — evidence that Fed expectations and positioning outweighed the support lower yields normally provide.

Silver and the wider metals sell-off

The weakness was not confined to gold. Early trading cited in market coverage showed silver down about 2.6% to $56.44 in one reading, alongside falls in platinum and palladium, before Kitco's U.S. morning reading put silver lower still. For industrial metals, higher borrowing costs and worries about activity add a second headwind on top of the gold-led sell-off.

Technically, FXStreet said gold had tumbled below the lower Bollinger Band near $4,063, with the 20-period moving average around $4,151 acting as resistance. A clear break below $4,063 could expose the $4,000 psychological mark, followed by June lows around $3,950, it said. Kitco gave a similar map: first support at $4,079 and $4,068, with resistance at $4,124.25 and $4,143.48.

What's next

Friday brings preliminary October purchasing managers' indexes and the final University of Michigan consumer sentiment survey. The bigger tests come next week: the Fed decision on October 27-28, followed on October 29 by the September personal consumption expenditures price index, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge. Policymakers will decide before they see that PCE report.

If crude stays elevated and the Fed signals December tightening, the path toward $4,000 stays open. If energy prices ease and yields retreat, gold has room to recover toward the $4,150 area — but until then, rallies are likely to meet selling.
